note: Size baselines for the shipped ExtendScript artifacts. `core` is the ES5 bundle produced by build:extendscript; `assembled` is dist/all2html.js — json2 + core + exporter.jsx — which is the file users actually install, and which had no budget at all until 2026-07-24; `afterEffects` is dist/after-effects/all2html-ae.jsx, which had no budget at all until it stopped being a standalone hand-written .jsx and started concatenating a real bundle (D13). test/integration/extendscript-bundle.test.ts prints current size, delta against `bytes`, and how much of the tolerance the delta consumes on every run, and fails when an artifact grows more than growthTolerance above `bytes`. Sub-tolerance growth is allowed but never silent: any nonzero delta is reported as UNATTRIBUTED DRIFT, because that is how 3,752 B (69% of the core allowance) was spent between the 2026-07-24 records without anyone deciding to spend it. Re-recording is a deliberate, reviewed commit: the last `history` entry must state the new `bytes`, and the test fails if it does not match. Measured with removeComments:true in tsconfig.extendscript.json — that stays on because comments are dead weight in a shipped artifact, not because the budget depends on it.

history.reason: First recorded baseline, replacing a fixed 102,400-byte cliff that had already been breached mid-session at 103,592 B.

+3,945 B (+4.0%) for the escaping and injection fixes: single-sourced escape module, escapeStyleContent, escapeScriptContent, isSafeUrl scheme allowlist, and CSS font-family validation. Deliberate — this closed two confirmed XSS holes (</style> breakout via font mappings, and the <!--<script> document swallow). Re-recorded rather than trimmed further: the implementation was already optimized twice to fit under the old cliff, and squeezing harder would have traded real safety for bytes.

+7,089 B (+6.9%) for structured warnings and surface capability declarations (SPEC 12.5 / 12.7). Breakdown measured in the built bundle: 1,565 B Illustrator capability declaration, 3,529 B declaration checker, 1,162 B structured-warning module, ~830 B of call-site codes. Deliberate: this is what makes 30 silently-dead settings cells warn instead of no-oping, including `output: multiple-files` and `imageFormat: svg` on Illustrator. Trimmed first rather than re-recorded first — the feature tables were split out of SurfaceCapabilities and the browser declaration was rewritten from an IIFE to a literal so rollup could tree-shake the non-Illustrator surfaces, together worth ~2.8 KB. What remains is the declaration prose users read in the warning and the checker itself; cutting either would trade the fix for bytes.

-4,954 B net (-4.5%), and the first entry that both attributes prior drift and reclaims. Attribution of the 3,752 B that had accumulated above 109,260 without a record (69% of the tolerance, spent silently): +2,111 B core/json-purity.js, now on the ExtendScript path at the resolve and emitter-ready boundaries where it previously had zero coverage (D21); +458 B emitters/shared/lazy-video.ts, the single-sourced video lazy-loading warning both HTML emitters call (D31); the residual ~1,183 B is the divergesAtDefault comparison in the capability checker plus the widened Figma/CLI declarations (D25). SETTING_DEFINITIONS is imported by schema.ts, defaults.ts and core/capabilities.ts, so it reaches the bundle, and rollup cannot tree-shake properties out of object literals inside an array literal — every byte of panel-only copy shipped into Illustrator. Only the CEP panel and scripts/generate-settings-docs.ts read it, and neither is in the ExtendScript entry graph. The prior note estimated ~11.8 KB from source bytes; the real bundled cost was 8,706 B. The test now asserts the bundle contains no help copy, so it cannot creep back in.

+1,683 B (+1.6%) for src/core/artboard-dimensions.ts, the input guard that closes the stringified-sentinel gap in D21. Attributed rather than absorbed. The entry+exit purity assertions were claimed to catch every sentinel reaching the emitter; they do not. compute-positions.ts divides by artboard width/height and immediately stringifies, so `width: 0` produced `left:Infinity%` with zero warnings on the ExtendScript path, which has no Zod validation — the exact path the guard exists for. Rejecting suspicious strings at the boundary was considered and refused: the walk covers user text, so it would throw on a chart label reading "NaN" or an artboard named "Infinity Pool". Artboard width/height are the only divisors in the ExtendScript-bound transforms, so validating them at entry covers the whole class.

+788 B (+0.7%) for the one-emitter collapse (SPEC 12.6 / D23): html.ts and html-string.ts became one builder (emitters/html-tree.ts) over a serializable node tree plus one ES3-safe serializer (emitters/shared/html-node.ts). Measured as rollup renderedLength: the old html-string.js was 19,693 B; html-tree.js + html-node.js are 20,481 B. Growth rather than reclaim, and the reason is that this bundle only ever carried ONE of the two duplicated emitters — the string one, in which the builder and the serializer were fused, so nothing here was duplicated to delete. What the 788 B buys inside Illustrator specifically: attribute order is now a property of the data (an array of pairs) rather than of Object.keys iteration order, which ES3 does not define and which this bundle's for-in polyfill therefore left unspecified; and the </script / </style neutralizations and all four escaping grammars now live in the serializer, so no future call site in the ExtendScript path can forget one. Repo-wide the change removes 239 lines and a whole parallel implementation. Reclaim was considered and refused: the only material savings available were re-fusing the serializer back into the builder or returning attributes to object literals, which is exactly the duplication and the unspecified ordering the change exists to remove.

-237 B (-0.2%). Reclaim. `GOOGLE_FONTS_LINK_MARKER` and `stripGoogleFontsLinkTags()` were removed from emitters/shared/google-fonts.ts. The marker existed so the Svelte and React emitters could regex the font `<link>` tags back out of serialized HTML; since the one-emitter collapse those emitters consume the node tree and never build the links at all (shared/component-tree.ts carries the href out separately), so nothing had read the attribute since. Illustrator paid for it twice: the constant and the dead stripper in the bundle, and a `data-all2html-google-fonts="true"` attribute on every `<link>` in every exported page with `googleFonts: "link"`.

+2,453 B (+2.3%), measured in two parts. +1,610 B: isValidCssFontFamily in compute-styles.ts is now a linear hand-written scan instead of a regex. The regex it replaced hung Illustrator — a single .test() against `arial,helvetica,sans-serif` did not finish in 300s, so every export using a mapped font was unusable, while V8 answered the same call in 56us and the whole suite passed. The replacement is byte-identical in behavior over a 200k-input fuzz against the old pattern, and test/integration/extendscript-regex-safety.test.ts now fails the build on any nested-quantifier regex in a shipped artifact. Bytes were not negotiable here: the alternative was a correct regex, and no regex of this grammar is safe on that engine. +843 B: per-transform phase timing in extendscript/index.ts, reported through the diagnostics hook. That is what localized the hang to computeStyles; without it the core is one opaque span and the Node reproduction is clean, so the bug looks like it is somewhere else.

223288 B. +4,232 B (+1.9%), 39% of tolerance. +84 B is carried from the core (see its entry). The remaining +4,148 B is plugins/illustrator/exporter.jsx: normalizeIllustratorInputs, the single boundary where untyped Illustrator input becomes typed exporter input. Three sources reach this exporter with no schema -- all2html.config.json (JSON.parse), the CEP panel settings and font payloads, and document text blocks -- and their values were read straight into typed operations at nine separate call sites, each with its own ad-hoc rule or none. Four defects were reproduced through the fake-DOM harness before the change: non-string font family/weight/style/vshift persisted into ir.json and rejected by loadAndValidateIR; the same malformed family crashing getPrimaryCssFamily with google_fonts: link; structural metadata values persisting an object in metadata.credit; and project_name: 42 crashing makeKeyword with no ir.json written at all. project_name is the case that shows why a font-only or metadata-only fix was refused: it IS a canonical setting, covered by SETTING_DEFINITIONS, and still failed because the raw value reached makeKeyword at the slug site BEFORE buildCanonicalIrSettings ran. That split also made project_name: null emit null.html while metadata.slug said countries -- one input normalized twice, naming two different artifacts. The defect class is therefore not 'fonts' or 'non-setting config keys' but 'an untyped input consumed by a typed operation before the exporter normalized it once'. After this call runExporter reads no raw docSettings key and no raw font entry: IR construction, output-path selection (resolveDocumentOutputPath now takes the validated canonical bag, so a path the settings boundary rejected can no longer choose where the run writes), image export, processAndEmit, cache-bust handling and the result envelope all consume inputs. readStringSetting rejects non-strings instead of String()-ing them, which is what closed project_name. inputs.settings IS the canonical bag, built and sanitized inside the boundary rather than copied, so this stays one validated settings object rather than reintroducing the two bags entry 218443 eliminated. Roughly 1.9 KB of the delta is comment -- exporter.jsx is concatenated verbatim -- already trimmed once from 5,396 B total. Reclaim was considered and REFUSED at one specific site: deleting the fonts override passed to processAndEmit looks like a provable identity since both arrays are the same normalized input, but mergeFonts replaces the FIRST entry matching a sourceFont, so with duplicate source fonts in one config the merged table is not the base table and dropping the override would silently change which family a duplicate resolves to. Not a byte of this is the new coverage: test/helpers/illustrator-fake-dom.ts now finds ir.json by basename in the recorded writes rather than reconstructing the path from envelope.outputPath -- the error path omits that field, so every ir.json written by a run that later threw was invisible to the harness, which is exactly the run most likely to have persisted a malformed document -- and validates every persisted IR through loadAndValidateIR inside the runner itself, so no test can opt out. 21 new scenarios pin the declared policy; reverting readStringSetting, the font family normalization, the metadata policy or the output-path source each turns this file red.

227329 B. +4,041 B (+1.8%) across the contract-cleanup branch: +849 B carried from the core (see its entry) and +3,192 B in plugins/illustrator/exporter.jsx, in four parts. It now concatenates json2 (as a string), the player template (as a string), dist/extendscript/all2html-ae-core.js and exporter.jsx, and the bundle is the part that can grow without anyone deciding to spend it.
